title: Twelve classrooms refitted in Palghar district
summary: Our site teams rebuilt furniture, lighting and ventilation across three zilla parishad schools during the monsoon shutdown, reaching 640 students.
body: Three zilla parishad schools in Palghar had classrooms with broken benches, single-bulb lighting and no cross-ventilation. Over eleven weeks our site teams stripped and rebuilt twelve rooms, working through the monsoon shutdown when project sites were idle.

Every bench and desk was built in the Bhiwandi workshop from timber recovered from project offcuts, finished in the same low-VOC lacquer we specify for client work. Lighting was replaced with LED battens on a separate circuit so classrooms remain usable during load-shedding.
Teachers asked for storage more than anything else, so each room received a full-height cupboard with a lockable base. The schools now hold 640 students across the twelve rooms.

title: Fourth apprentice intake joins the joinery programme
partner: With the Maharashtra State Skill Development Society
summary: Twenty-four apprentices began an eighteen-month paid joinery programme at the Bhiwandi workshop, with a guaranteed interview at the end of it.
body: The joinery apprenticeship pairs each intake with a senior carpenter for eighteen months. Apprentices are paid from day one, rotate through machining, assembly, finishing and site installation, and sit a practical assessment every quarter.
Of the 68 apprentices who have completed the programme since 2021, 51 are still working in the trade and 34 are on the Fabluxora Interiors payroll.
This intake is the first to include a dedicated finishing module, added after supervisors flagged that spray finishing was the hardest skill to hire for.

title: 1,800 native saplings planted along the Ulhas corridor
summary: A two-weekend planting drive with 120 staff volunteers, using only species native to the catchment and a three-year maintenance contract.
body: Planting drives fail when nobody waters the saplings in year two. This one was funded with a three-year maintenance contract attached, paid to a local self-help group that also handles the guards and mulching.
Species were chosen with Vanarai Trust from the catchment's native list — karanj, jamun, bahava and arjun — with no ornamental imports.
Survival at the twelve-month count was 81%, and gaps have been replanted.

title: Upholstery unit set up with a women's collective in Nashik
summary: Fourteen artisans now run a working upholstery unit that supplies soft furnishings to Fabluxora projects at commercial rates.
body: This is procurement, not charity. Fabluxe funded machines, tables and six weeks of training; the collective owns the unit and invoices us at market rates like any other supplier.
The unit produces cushions, headboards and loose covers, and has taken on work from two other Nashik studios since opening.
Fourteen artisans are on the books, nine of them earning a regular monthly income for the first time.

title: Refurbished appliances placed in 42 community kitchens
summary: Working appliances collected under our take-back scheme were tested, refurbished by service engineers and placed in community kitchens.
body: Our take-back scheme collects the appliance being replaced at every installation. Most go to a registered e-waste recycler, but a proportion still work perfectly.
Service engineers tested and refurbished 118 units on their own time, backed by a company-funded parts budget, and the working stock went to 42 community kitchens across Mumbai and Pune.
Each kitchen also received a twelve-month service commitment so a small fault does not put the unit back out of use.

title: Site safety and heat-stress training for 380 workers
partner: With the Nirman Workers Welfare Board
summary: Every worker on a Fabluxe site — employed or contracted — completed a paid day of safety and heat-stress training ahead of the summer.
body: Contract workers are usually left out of safety training because nobody wants to pay for their day. We paid for it: 380 workers, employed and contracted alike, completed a full day before the summer peak.
The heat-stress module set mandatory shade, water and rest cycles for sites above 38°C, and gave any worker the right to stop work without loss of pay.
Reportable incidents across our sites fell from nine in 2024 to two in 2025.
